# Bylda

> Bylda is a commercial behavior intelligence platform for revenue teams. It sits
> on top of the CRM a team already runs — Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive,
> Dynamics — and watches how deals actually unfold across calls, email, calendar,
> and CRM activity. It keeps the CRM current automatically, identifies the
> behavior affecting revenue (objections, stakeholder changes, engagement shifts,
> seller actions), and tells the team what to do next. It is not a CRM and not a
> dashboard.

## The core idea

Traditional sales software is organized around records: account, contact,
opportunity, stage, amount, activity, notes. But revenue does not happen because
a CRM field changes — it happens through behavior. A buyer raises a pricing
concern and the seller answers with a discount instead of resolving the
objection. A champion stops responding. Procurement enters before the economic
buyer has engaged. A decision timeline slips.

CRM systems record what sales teams say happened. Bylda learns what actually
happened, why it happened, and what the team should do next.

Traditional CRM = system of record. Bylda = system of commercial behavior.

## What it does today

- **Captures commercial activity** across Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams, plus email, calendar, and CRM activity. No notetaker bot joins the room.
- **Understands behavior, not keywords** — objections and whether they were resolved, stakeholder involvement, engagement shifts, urgency, buying signals, seller behavior, timing, and deal risk.
- **Writes the CRM automatically** — around 14 fields per call into Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, or Microsoft Dynamics, two-way and in real time, custom fields included. Every write is traceable to a timestamp, logged, and reversible.
- **Recommends the next action** with its evidence, reviewed by the rep before it executes.
- **Drafts follow-ups** in each rep's own voice, referencing the specifics of the conversation.
- **Prepares a daily brief** for reps and leaders: what changed, why it matters, what to do.

## Where Bylda is going (not shipped)

Clearly marked as vision, not current capability: calibrated behavioral models,
intervention analysis, commercial experimentation, scenario analysis, and
eventually helping teams test commercial decisions before deploying them. Bylda
does not claim perfect sales prediction, causal attribution it has not validated,
digital twins, production simulated markets, guaranteed revenue uplift, or
autonomous revenue optimization. See https://usebylda.com/vision.

## Key facts

- Category: commercial behavior intelligence (behavioral deal intelligence + CRM automation + execution)
- Long-term category framing: the behavioral operating system for revenue
- Pricing: Phantom $89 per rep/month, Team $129 per rep/month, Enterprise custom. 20% off annually.
- Minimum: 5 seats on Phantom and Team, 50 on Enterprise.
- Implementation: most teams are live in an afternoon. No data migration.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, SSO/SAML and SCIM, US/EU/UK data residency, GDPR and CCPA, HIPAA BAA on request.
- Model training: customer conversations are never used to train shared or third-party models.
- Typical results: about 6.5 hours per rep per week returned; CRM required-field completeness from roughly 41% to above 95% in a quarter.

## How it differs

- **Versus a CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot):** a CRM stores what a human types. Bylda does the typing and understands the behavior underneath it. You keep your CRM — Bylda is not a replacement and requires no migration.
- **Versus conversation intelligence (e.g. Gong):** the call is the unit of analysis there. For Bylda the deal's behavior over time is the unit — the call connected to the follow-up, the stakeholders, the CRM state, and the outcome.
- **Versus revenue/forecasting platforms (e.g. Clari):** those analyse what is already in the CRM, so accuracy is bounded by what reps entered. Bylda works upstream, writing the record from observed activity.

## Writing

- [CRM data vs sales behavior: what's the difference?](https://usebylda.com/blog/crm-data-vs-sales-behavior) (2026-09-10): The record is a lossy compression of the behavior, and the parts it discards — sequence, absence, change, and the seller's own actions — are the parts that predict outcomes.
- [How to identify a deal at risk before it stalls](https://usebylda.com/blog/how-to-identify-a-deal-at-risk) (2026-09-10): Six behavioral signals that predict a stall weeks before the close date moves, and what to do about each.
- [Why sales forecasts fail when CRM data is stale](https://usebylda.com/blog/why-sales-forecasts-fail-with-stale-crm-data) (2026-09-10): Forecast error is inherited from hand-authored records with a systematic optimism bias — it compounds rather than cancels out.
- [What an AI Sales Operating System actually is](https://usebylda.com/blog/ai-sales-operating-system) (2026-07-14): CRM is a database. Conversation intelligence is a recorder. The layer between them does the work.
- [CRM adoption was never a training problem](https://usebylda.com/blog/crm-adoption-was-never-a-training-problem) (2026-06-28): Twenty years of enablement and required fields have not fixed CRM data quality.
- [Conversation intelligence is not the product](https://usebylda.com/blog/conversation-intelligence-is-not-the-product) (2026-06-09): The value was never in the insight — it was in whether anything happened next.
- [Five CRM automation workflows worth building](https://usebylda.com/blog/crm-automation-workflows) (2026-05-19): The five workflows that actually return time, and the order to build them in.
- [How to automate sales follow-ups](https://usebylda.com/blog/how-to-automate-follow-ups) (2026-04-22): Automating the work while keeping every message specific.
